**Considering design parameters**

I'm working on preserving the existing wall thickness at the end bosses. I should define the original hole diameter as D_old and the outer terminal boss diameter as D_outer_old. The radial wall thickness is calculated as (D_outer - D_old) / 2. For the new diameters, D_new will be D_old + 1, and D_outer_new will be D_new + 2t, giving me an updated D_outer_old + 1. I’m determining that a constant arm width will match D_outer_new. This will help with stiffness, as it aligns with the design envelope.
**Ensuring operational details**

I need to include all relevant operational details. For Operation 1, the target features include arm bodies and bore features, with broad faces. There are four steps plus a fillet involved. operations_plan.summary: Replace the four scissor-link outer silhouettes with continuous long-hole-shaped (obround/capsule) profiles while preserving each arm's two terminal pivot centers, intermediate crossing-pivot center, thickness, axial placement, and existing holes. The capsule width is initially derived from the existing terminal boss diameter so the narrow connecting portions gain material and stiffness.

steps.description: Measure and parameterize the existing link geometry. Extract the axes and center coordinates of all terminal and central pivot bores from cylindrical faces 26, 25, and 27 for the front descending arm; 157, 155, and 156 for the front ascending arm; 185, 184, and 186 for the rear descending arm; and 215, 213, and 214 for the rear ascending arm. For each arm, define its longitudinal capsule centerline through the two terminal bore centers and verify that the central bore center lies on that line. Record the original arm thickness, front/rear extrusion limits, terminal boss outer diameter, bore diameters, and perimeter fillet radius. Keep all extracted centers and axes fixed as master references for subsequent operations.

Reshape the front descending arm. Create or edit a sketch on the plane of broad face 24, using the upper-left terminal bore axis from face 26 and lower-right terminal bore axis from face 27 as the capsule endpoints. Construct two parallel tangent sides joined by semicircular ends, producing one continuous obround outline. Set the initial capsule width W0 equal to the measured existing terminal-boss outer diameter, eliminating the separate-looking central boss and narrow strips while retaining the central pivot at face 25. Replace only the arm's external material envelope, extrude symmetrically to the original thickness and axial limits, and retain the three coaxial bore openings. Do not move the upper slider, center crossing, or lower fixed-pivot axes.

Reshape the front ascending arm in the same manner. Sketch on broad face 154, place the capsule endpoints concentrically with the lower-left bore face 157 and upper-right bore face 156, and constrain the straight sides parallel to the line joining those axes. Use the same initial width W0 as the corresponding existing terminal bosses, retain the central crossing axis from face 155, and replace the old boss-and-strip outline with a continuous capsule extruded to the unchanged arm thickness and front-side axial position.

Reshape the rear descending arm as a mirror-equivalent capsule. Create or edit the profile sketch on outer broad face 171, with capsule endpoints at the upper-left bore axis from face 185 and lower-right bore axis from face 186. Retain the center axis from face 184, use the measured terminal-boss diameter as W0, and extrude the new profile between the original rear arm broad-face limits. Preserve the rear layer's axial offset and clearance from the red beams and front linkage.

Reshape the rear ascending arm as a mirror-equivalent capsule. Sketch on outer broad face 200, use the lower-left bore axis from face 215 and upper-right bore axis from face 214 as the rounded-end centers, and retain the center crossing axis from face 213. Apply the initial width W0 and the original arm thickness and axial position so the rear layer remains aligned with the front layer through the common terminal pins.

Apply perimeter edge blends to the rebuilt capsule bodies using the measured original arm fillet radius, or the largest smaller radius permitted by the unchanged arm thickness if the original value cannot regenerate. Blend only the longitudinal outer edges; do not fillet or displace the cylindrical pivot bores. Ensure the capsule profiles on corresponding front and rear arms are geometrically mirrored and that no new material crosses into the beam bodies at the current linkage position.

operations_plan.summary: Increase every terminal and central pivot bore in all four link arms by 1 mm in total diameter while preserving all bore centers, joint axes, arm thicknesses, and coaxial relationships. The request does not state the direction or subset explicitly; this plan resolves it as a +1 mm diametric increase applied to all twelve link-arm bores, without changing the pins or beam bores.

steps.description: Define the revised bore parameter for each applicable arm hole as D_new = D_original + 1.00 mm, corresponding to a radial enlargement of 0.50 mm. Apply the change to all end and central holes because the request refers generally to the holes in the link arms. Keep the original cylinder axes, center coordinates, and through-all direction. Treat the unspecified direction of change as an unresolved input resolved by the explicit assumption of an increase; if design authority later specifies a decrease, substitute D_new = D_original - 1.00 mm without changing any centers.

Enlarge the three bores of the front descending arm concentrically. Edit the bore dimensions represented by cylindrical faces 26, 25, and 27, or subtract three coaxial through-cylinders of diameter D_new through the complete arm thickness if direct feature editing is unavailable. Preserve the upper-left sliding-pivot, central crossing-pivot, and lower-right fixed-pivot center positions exactly.

Enlarge the three bores of the front ascending arm concentrically from cylindrical faces 157, 155, and 156 to D_new. Make each cut through the complete existing arm thickness, retain the lower-left slider, center crossing, and upper-right fixed-pivot axes, and do not alter the axial stacking relationship between the two front arms.

Enlarge the three bores of the rear descending arm concentrically from cylindrical faces 185, 184, and 186 to D_new. Preserve exact coaxial alignment with the corresponding front-link terminal pin axes and retain the rear central crossing axis independently of the front center pin.

Enlarge the three bores of the rear ascending arm concentrically from cylindrical faces 215, 213, and 214 to D_new. Preserve the lower-left slider, center crossing, and upper-right fixed-pivot locations and the original rear-layer axial position.

Verify that the enlarged arm bores remain coaxial with their existing mating pins and beam joint axes. Preserve the upper and lower beam bores, guide slots, and all pins because increasing an arm bore does not require larger mating hardware and only increases radial clearance by 0.50 mm. Flag the resulting additional joint clearance for engineering review if the mechanism requires a specified bearing fit.

operations_plan.summary: Adjust the new long-hole-shaped arm profiles to compensate for the 1 mm bore enlargement, preserving the original radial edge distance around the joints where practical, then validate linkage clearances and kinematics.

steps.description: Calculate the original minimum radial ligament between each pivot bore and its surrounding terminal or central boss envelope. Define the final capsule width W_final so every enlarged bore retains at least that original minimum ligament. For equal original bore sizes and equal boss diameters, use W_final = W0 + 1.00 mm and final capsule end radius R_final = W_final/2 = R0 + 0.50 mm. If measured bore sizes differ, use one constant capsule width equal to the maximum value of D_new + 2 times the preserved minimum ligament so the profile remains a true long-hole shape.

Update the four capsule sketches to W_final while holding both terminal pivot centers and the longitudinal centerline fixed. Offset each straight side outward by the required radial adjustment, nominally 0.50 mm, and enlarge both semicircular end radii by the same amount. Maintain tangent continuity between straight sides and rounded ends. The central holes must remain centered on the capsule centerlines with no separate external center boss.

Regenerate the four arm solids at their unchanged thicknesses and axial locations, then reapply the original perimeter fillet radius to the revised outer edges. Confirm that no edge blend breaks into an enlarged bore; where necessary, reduce only the local fillet radius while preserving the final capsule width and minimum bore ligament.

Run static interference and minimum-clearance checks for the revised arm envelopes against the upper and lower beam bodies, guide-slot boundaries, fixed and sliding pins, the opposite arm in each scissor layer, and the mirrored linkage layer. Preserve the existing arm stacking and axial offsets. If the nominal 0.50 mm outward profile growth causes interference, locally limit the profile only in the conflicting region using tangent transitions while retaining the greatest feasible ligament; do not move pivot centers, alter beam geometry, or change arm thickness.

Validate the mechanism through its available scissor travel. Keep the four terminal joint axes on their original paths, with the left upper and lower axes translating only within their existing horizontal slots and the right upper and lower axes remaining fixed. Confirm free relative rotation at every enlarged arm bore, adequate edge distance throughout the four capsule profiles, no collision between crossed arms, and unchanged upper-to-lower platform alignment. Do not modify the red beams, slot dimensions, pin axes, or center-to-center link lengths during validation.

operations_plan.summary: Replace the four scissor-link outer silhouettes with continuous long-hole-shaped (obround/capsule) profiles while preserving each arm's two terminal pivot centers, intermediate crossing-pivot center, thickness, axial placement, and existing holes. The capsule width is initially derived from the existing terminal boss diameter so the narrow connecting portions gain material and stiffness.

steps.description: Measure and parameterize the existing link geometry. Extract the axes and center coordinates of all terminal and central pivot bores from cylindrical faces 26, 25, and 27 for the front descending arm; 157, 155, and 156 for the front ascending arm; 185, 184, and 186 for the rear descending arm; and 215, 213, and 214 for the rear ascending arm. For each arm, define its longitudinal capsule centerline through the two terminal bore centers and verify that the central bore center lies on that line. Record the original arm thickness, front/rear extrusion limits, terminal boss outer diameter, bore diameters, and perimeter fillet radius. Keep all extracted centers and axes fixed as master references for subsequent operations.

Reshape the front descending arm. Create or edit a sketch on the plane of broad face 24, using the upper-left terminal bore axis from face 26 and lower-right terminal bore axis from face 27 as the capsule endpoints. Construct two parallel tangent sides joined by semicircular ends, producing one continuous obround outline. Set the initial capsule width W0 equal to the measured existing terminal-boss outer diameter, eliminating the separate-looking central boss and narrow strips while retaining the central pivot at face 25. Replace only the arm's external material envelope, extrude symmetrically to the original thickness and axial limits, and retain the three coaxial bore openings. Do not move the upper slider, center crossing, or lower fixed-pivot axes.

Reshape the front ascending arm in the same manner. Sketch on broad face 154, place the capsule endpoints concentrically with the lower-left bore face 157 and upper-right bore face 156, and constrain the straight sides parallel to the line joining those axes. Use the same initial width W0 as the corresponding existing terminal bosses, retain the central crossing axis from face 155, and replace the old boss-and-strip outline with a continuous capsule extruded to the unchanged arm thickness and front-side axial position.

Reshape the rear descending arm as a mirror-equivalent capsule. Create or edit the profile sketch on outer broad face 171, with capsule endpoints at the upper-left bore axis from face 185 and lower-right bore axis from face 186. Retain the center axis from face 184, use the measured terminal-boss diameter as W0, and extrude the new profile between the original rear arm broad-face limits. Preserve the rear layer's axial offset and clearance from the red beams and front linkage.

Reshape the rear ascending arm as a mirror-equivalent capsule. Sketch on outer broad face 200, use the lower-left bore axis from face 215 and upper-right bore axis from face 214 as the rounded-end centers, and retain the center crossing axis from face 213. Apply the initial width W0 and the original arm thickness and axial position so the rear layer remains aligned with the front layer through the common terminal pins.

Apply perimeter edge blends to the rebuilt capsule bodies using the measured original arm fillet radius, or the largest smaller radius permitted by the unchanged arm thickness if the original value cannot regenerate. Blend only the longitudinal outer edges; do not fillet or displace the cylindrical pivot bores. Ensure the capsule profiles on corresponding front and rear arms are geometrically mirrored and that no new material crosses into the beam bodies at the current linkage position.

operations_plan.summary: Increase every terminal and central pivot bore in all four link arms by 1 mm in total diameter while preserving all bore centers, joint axes, arm thicknesses, and coaxial relationships. The request does not state the direction or subset explicitly; this plan resolves it as a +1 mm diametric increase applied to all twelve link-arm bores, without changing the pins or beam bores.

steps.description: Define the revised bore parameter for each applicable arm hole as D_new = D_original + 1.00 mm, corresponding to a radial enlargement of 0.50 mm. Apply the change to all end and central holes because the request refers generally to the holes in the link arms. Keep the original cylinder axes, center coordinates, and through-all direction. Treat the unspecified direction of change as an unresolved input resolved by the explicit assumption of an increase; if design authority later specifies a decrease, substitute D_new = D_original - 1.00 mm without changing any centers.

Enlarge the three bores of the front descending arm concentrically. Edit the bore dimensions represented by cylindrical faces 26, 25, and 27, or subtract three coaxial through-cylinders of diameter D_new through the complete arm thickness if direct feature editing is unavailable. Preserve the upper-left sliding-pivot, central crossing-pivot, and lower-right fixed-pivot center positions exactly.

Enlarge the three bores of the front ascending arm concentrically from cylindrical faces 157, 155, and 156 to D_new. Make each cut through the complete existing arm thickness, retain the lower-left slider, center crossing, and upper-right fixed-pivot axes, and do not alter the axial stacking relationship between the two front arms.

Enlarge the three bores of the rear descending arm concentrically from cylindrical faces 185, 184, and 186 to D_new. Preserve exact coaxial alignment with the corresponding front-link terminal pin axes and retain the rear central crossing axis independently of the front center pin.

Enlarge the three bores of the rear ascending arm concentrically from cylindrical faces 215, 213, and 214 to D_new. Preserve the lower-left slider, center crossing, and upper-right fixed-pivot locations and the original rear-layer axial position.

Verify that the enlarged arm bores remain coaxial with their existing mating pins and beam joint axes. Preserve the upper and lower beam bores, guide slots, and all pins because increasing an arm bore does not require larger mating hardware and only increases radial clearance by 0.50 mm. Flag the resulting additional joint clearance for engineering review if the mechanism requires a specified bearing fit.

operations_plan.summary: Adjust the new long-hole-shaped arm profiles to compensate for the 1 mm bore enlargement, preserving the original radial edge distance around the joints where practical, then validate linkage clearances and kinematics.

steps.description: Calculate the original minimum radial ligament between each pivot bore and its surrounding terminal or central boss envelope. Define the final capsule width W_final so every enlarged bore retains at least that original minimum ligament. For equal original bore sizes and equal boss diameters, use W_final = W0 + 1.00 mm and final capsule end radius R_final = W_final/2 = R0 + 0.50 mm. If measured bore sizes differ, use one constant capsule width equal to the maximum value of D_new + 2 times the preserved minimum ligament so the profile remains a true long-hole shape.

Update the four capsule sketches to W_final while holding both terminal pivot centers and the longitudinal centerline fixed. Offset each straight side outward by the required radial adjustment, nominally 0.50 mm, and enlarge both semicircular end radii by the same amount. Maintain tangent continuity between straight sides and rounded ends. The central holes must remain centered on the capsule centerlines with no separate external center boss.

Regenerate the four arm solids at their unchanged thicknesses and axial locations, then reapply the original perimeter fillet radius to the revised outer edges. Confirm that no edge blend breaks into an enlarged bore; where necessary, reduce only the local fillet radius while preserving the final capsule width and minimum bore ligament.

Run static interference and minimum-clearance checks for the revised arm envelopes against the upper and lower beam bodies, guide-slot boundaries, fixed and sliding pins, the opposite arm in each scissor layer, and the mirrored linkage layer. Preserve the existing arm stacking and axial offsets. If the nominal 0.50 mm outward profile growth causes interference, locally limit the profile only in the conflicting region using tangent transitions while retaining the greatest feasible ligament; do not move pivot centers, alter beam geometry, or change arm thickness.

Validate the mechanism through its available scissor travel. Keep the four terminal joint axes on their original paths, with the left upper and lower axes translating only within their existing horizontal slots and the right upper and lower axes remaining fixed. Confirm free relative rotation at every enlarged arm bore, adequate edge distance throughout the four capsule profiles, no collision between crossed arms, and unchanged upper-to-lower platform alignment. Do not modify the red beams, slot dimensions, pin axes, or center-to-center link lengths during validation.
